story.heading: Where Endurance Meets Adventure
paragraphs: Ultra Adventures races cross some of the most scenic and challenging trail in the Southwest, on the historic and sacred lands of Utah and Arizona's Grand Circle.
Now under the direction of Aravaipa Running, the series brings the Tushars back together with the Zion Ultras, Bryce Canyon Ultras and Antelope Canyon Ultras.

tribute.heading: Matt Gunn
paragraphs: None of this exists without Matt Gunn. Matt founded Ultra Adventures in 2012 with the Zion 100 and spent years building a series of races that opened up the Grand Circle to runners from around the world. His vision, his love for this region and his care for the people who came out to run it are the foundation of what Ultra Adventures was and what we build on today. We're honored to carry it forward.

history.heading: How the Series Grew
paragraphs: Ultra Adventures started with one race and grew into a season of destination ultras across the Grand Circle, the ring of national parks, tribal parks and monuments around the Utah and Arizona line. By late 2014 the races ran together as The Grand Circle Trail Series, with a zero waste promise at every event and a Trifecta Challenge that sent runners out to three must-see trails near each course.
The series also counted Behind the Rocks in Moab, put on by Mad Moose Events, in 2015 and 2016.

timeline.text: Bryce Canyon joins with a 100 mile and 100K.
Antelope Canyon, Monument Valley and Grand Canyon run for the first time.
Capitol Reef and the Tushars join the calendar.
The last Monument Valley and Grand Canyon races on record.
Zion, Bryce Canyon and Antelope Canyon carry on as Ultra Adventures races with Vacation Races.
Aravaipa Running brings Zion, Bryce Canyon, Antelope Canyon and the Tushars back together.

races.location: Kaibab National Forest, North Rim, AZ
races.text: Forest trail along the North Rim from Big Saddle Tank to the Crazy Jug, Monument Point, Thunder Mountain and Sowats Point overlooks.

races.name: Capitol Reef Ultras
races.text: From the red cliffs of Capitol Reef up onto the Aquarius Plateau, above 11,000 feet for nearly half the race, then back down to finish at Red River Ranch.
